thread.title: Apple: How a New iPhone Lineup Could Shake Up Sales

title: Apple: How a New iPhone Lineup Could Shake Up Sales
text:
Large Photo: Getty Images 
If Apple makes some of the changes in its iPhone lineup many expect, it could boost its average selling price and total phone revenues substantially if shipments grow 1.4%, according to Raymond James. 
According to a Friday note, based on assumptions about Apple’s (AAPL) lineup and the price that would go with it: We view Apple’s pricing strategy to be aimed at maximizing operating profit against the backdrop of somewhat mature iPhone unit demand. 
This is no longer about maximizing unit sales, since given iPhone penetration rates, we don’t think there’s much Apple could do at this point to substantially grow iPhone units. What they can do is to maximize the profit dollars they extract from each phone, by offering phones at a wider range of price points, and by convincing customers to purchase the most expensive iPhone they can afford. 
In a chart, the analysts illustrated how shipments, average selling price and revenue could change if Apple retires some phones and adds others, (They expect the current X will be sold down, three phones will be added, and the current 7 or 8 could come out of the lineup.) Illustration: Raymond James 
The upshot is an estimate of 1.4% shipment growth, an average selling price of $727, and revenue above $180 billion. (The average selling price on the chart is not weighted by product mix, which is why the revenue number isn’t the product of the ASP and the unit volume.) 
Apple, a Barron’s Next 50 component, was the number-two global seller of smartphones in 2017, according to IDC data, behind Samsung and after Huawei. It took the crown in the fourth quarter , however.
